title: Move iris scissors, a syringe and a medicine cup onto a sterile field with thumb forceps: tips only, no arm over it
instruction: Using the sterile forceps, move the scissors, the syringe and the medicine cup from the opened sterile pack onto the sterile field without contaminating anything, then lay the forceps back across the field's edge and let go.
context: Registered nurses (O*NET 29-1141.00; 3,465,400 employed in 2025; "Prepare rooms, sterile instruments, equipment, or supplies and ensure that stock of supplies is maintained.") and medical assistants (O*NET 31-9092.00; 833,900 employed in 2025), who prepare treatment rooms and hand physicians instruments and materials, set up a sterile field with bare hands before they glove. Sterile forceps are then the only thing that may touch sterile supplies. Doyle and McCutcheon, Clinical Procedures for Safer Patient Care (1.5, principles of sterile technique), gives the rules scored here: "Place large items on the sterile field using sterile gloves or sterile transfer forceps"; "the border of one inch at the edge of the sterile drape is considered non-sterile"; "a non-sterile person should not reach over a sterile field"; "Keep the tips of forceps down". The grippers are the bare hands: the robot works the forceps as a tool, reaches in from the edge, and each item needs a different hold.
setup: Cm from the midpoint between the arm bases, x away from the robot, y left; heights above the table, which stands in for a treatment-room counter. Sterile field, fixed: a stainless Mayo instrument tray (49 x 32.5 x 1.9 cm) under a blue sterile drape, a block 32.5 (x) by 49 (y) by 2.0 cm, near edge at x 33.0, y -17.0 to 32.0. Sterile pack, fixed: an opened sterilization wrapper, light blue, 30.5 x 30.5 cm, 2 mm thick, lying flat, inside up, near edge at x 33.0, y -51.5 to -21.0. On the pack, loose: (1) straight stainless iris scissors, 11.5 cm (4.5 in), closed, 20 g, lying flat, finger rings toward the robot, points away and 15 degrees to the left (their left shank then points straight away): screw at (44.2, -27.7), back of the rings at (37.4, -29.5), points at (48.5, -26.5); rings of 3.5 mm round bar, each 2.6 x 2.2 cm outside, 4.8 cm across both; shanks 3.5 mm wide, 3 mm thick. (2) A 1 mL polypropylene luer slip syringe without needle, plunger pushed in, 2 g: barrel 6.9 mm across and 6.8 cm long, 9.3 cm overall, finger flange 2.0 x 1.1 cm; it lies along x, thumb rest toward the robot at x 36.8, tip at x 46.1, axis at y -44.5. (3) A stainless-steel 2 oz (59 ml) graduated medicine cup: 5.1 cm across the rolled rim, 4.45 cm tall, 3.7 cm across the base, 35 g, standing with its middle at (38.5, -37.5). Sterile thumb dressing forceps, loose: stainless, 14 cm (5.5 in), serrated tips, 25 g, tips 15 mm apart at rest, about 2.5 N at the finger grip to close them. They lie on edge (the two blades side by side, 11 mm tall) along x at y -12.5: tail at x 28.0, so the handle sticks 5 cm out over the field's near edge, tips at x 42.0 on the field. Both arms start in their rest pose; no part of them is over the field or the pack. Second layout (XFER_LOT=B): scissors' screw at (44.5, -27.0), same heading; syringe from x 37.2, axis y -38.0; cup at (39.0, -44.0); forceps at y -12.0. Sterile: the three items, the 5 cm of the forceps from their tips, and the tops of the field and the pack more than 2.5 cm from their edges. Not sterile: the grippers and arms, the table, both 2.5 cm borders, the tray's sides, and the 6.5 cm of the forceps from their tail.
scoring: Scored at the end from what touched what during the trial (video, and a ruler for the borders). Touching means within 1.5 mm; 4 mm for any part of an arm. A sterile thing is contaminated when it touches the table, a 2.5 cm border, the tray's side, an arm, the forceps' handle (the 6.5 cm from the tail) or anything already contaminated. The field or the pack is also contaminated when any part of an arm is above its sterile part at any height; the forceps' working end (the 5 cm from the tips) also when, while the forceps are held (an arm within 3 cm of them), the tips are more than 5 mm higher than the handle's end. 0 if the field is contaminated. Otherwise 0.25 for one item, 0.5 for two and 0.75 for all three that rest on the field's sterile part: every part of the item inside the border; the cup upright within 10 degrees; the scissors and the syringe lying with no part more than 2.5 cm above the field; uncontaminated, let go (arms 3 cm away, forceps' tips 2 cm away) and at rest (under 2 cm/s). 1.0: all three, and the forceps put down, let go (arms 3 cm away), at rest and uncontaminated, with their whole working end resting on the sterile part of the field or the pack.
reset_notes: Put the scissors, the syringe and the cup back on their marks on the pack and lay the forceps across the field's edge. Nothing is consumed; on a real rig the items, forceps, drape and wrapper are treated as sterile by convention at the start of each trial.
fidelity: Rigid parts at full size; no cloth, so gauze and cotton balls are left out. Catalogue sizes: forceps and scissors lengths, cup, tray, syringe barrel. Estimates: ring, shank and flange shapes, all masses, the forceps' closing force. The 2 g syringe is a 10 g body with 8 g of its weight carried by a steady force (for the solver); its plunger does not move. Touching is judged by distance, once per control step, over the arms' whole collision shapes. Not tried on a physical rig.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0; demo: 1.0 (the demo video and the setup picture show the overhead camera beside the right wrist camera)
